newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriots, fearing second quake, leave buildings.
newsitem.headline: Cypriots, fearing second quake, leave buildings.

text.p: Office workers evacuated buildings in the Cypriot capital Nicosia on Thursday, fearing a repeat of a powerful tremor measuring 6.3 on the Richter scale that rocked the island on Wednesday but caused little damage.
People went into the streets after hearing rumours, fuelled by a local radio station, that a bigger quake was imminent.
Government seismologists said that although aftershocks were expected there was nothing to suggest that an earthquake larger than the initial one would occur.
Government spokesman Yiannakis Cassoulides appealed for calm and told people not to heed rumours.
The initial earthquake had an epicentre about 40 km southwest of the coastal resort of Paphos. It was felt throughout the Middle East.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) was unaffected, increasing 0.07 percent to close at 83.94.
